items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: He came off a circus and came with us.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, they were real tight all their life. That's right.
And then we had Titty-Tat a while. Yeah, Tatt. What's Titty-Tat right now? Now, that's a man was playing bop on the trumpet in the 20s. He was, how many years, about 40 years ahead of time.

items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: Adolf Alexander's Tat. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, that's his name.

ctx.x: And by me being in New Orleans, every day, I could contact Harold, mostly any time I want, I used to catch him by the Whitney Bank. By the Whitney Bank, yeah. Yeah, because I used to carry a railroad mail there all the time. That's right. Yeah. So we worked together for many, many years, I'll put it to that. And, uh, yeah. And when Harold couldn't come, that's how Tat came into the picture. Yeah, I said Tat. He sent Tat once or twice. Who's Tat? Adolf Alexander. Are you trying to think of his name? Adolf…

items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: He came off a circus and came with us... With Alphonse? With Trent, yeah, with the big orchestra.

ctx.x: Oh, Titty-Tat. I can think of his name. Where is he from? New Orleans. No, Titty-Tat, Titty-Tat's from New Orleans. Oh, Titty-Tat. I'm talking about Titty-Tat. The trumpet. The trumpet was living on Mount Main. Hot doggie. Used to keep the name. Yeah, he played it upside down. And then he used to play that Titty-Tit-Tat, you know, that box trumpet. In other words. 40 years ago. He was on a circus type. Yeah, it was a circus type. A circus type playing. Yes, sir. He came off a circus and came with us. That man…

Yeah. Red Island was playing a lot of flatted fifths back in 1929. I got records of that and all that stuff, you know. Higginbotham Blues, the ends of a flatted fifth in 1929. That's what J.C. Higginbotham was playing. He was out of that Louis Russell group, you know.
